name: Acadiana (Louisiana, United States)
description: A field parted per pall with the apex at the fly: a white triangle at the hoist bearing a gold star, a navy panel above with three white fleurs-de-lis, and a red panel below with a gold castle.
history: Designed in 1965 by Thomas J. Arceneaux of the University of Southwestern Louisiana as the flag of the 22-parish Cajun heartland, officially recognized by Louisiana in 1974. The fleurs-de-lis recall Bourbon France, the castle Spanish Castile — Louisiana's two colonial mothers — and the gold star on white, like Acadia's flag, is Our Lady of the Assumption, patroness of the Acadians.

features.role: white hoist triangle parting a navy upper and red lower field

features.symbolism: Our Lady of the Assumption, patroness of the Acadians
